clue.text: Damn the two of them, getting European allowance

parts.note: both means the two of them together
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: Someone curses a pair of people who have both been granted a European subsidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Botheration is an old-fashioned exclamation of annoyance, used just like the mild curse damn.

clue.text: Fruit mountains after the first of October

indicators.note: after says the mountains come behind the October letter
the first of picks the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: ranges are chains of mountains

explanation.surface: Fruit piles up from the start of October.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruit.

clue.text: Tricky problem — damaged tooth needs a crown put back in

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed piece sits inside the scrambled tooth letters
damaged means broken, so these letters are rearranged
put back means turned round, so the piece is read backwards

parts.note: the crown of something is its top

explanation.surface: A dentist's headache: a broken tooth needing a crown fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives HOTTO, 'put back' gives POTA, and 'in' places it after the first three letters; the dental surface hides the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue that is awkward to handle.

clue.text: Head of school involved in knocks and scrapes

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the letter goes within the knocks word

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A headmaster gets caught up in fights and scuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a harsh grating sound or action, so rasps are scrapes.

clue.text: Faith expressed in being tied up

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word for faith is heard aloud

parts.note: trust means faith

explanation.surface: Faith being bound up in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in being' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means bound tightly, as a chicken is before roasting.

clue.text: Eccentric's love doubled outside dance

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: outside picks the letters at the outer edges of the word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An odd person's passion, twice over, outside a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' looks like an instruction to repeat, but is the word whose outer letters, D and D, are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is a strange or unconventional person, an eccentric.

clue.text: Rule leaves volatile fund managers in trouble?

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves means departs, so the rule letter is removed

explanation.surface: Unstable investment managers break the rules and get into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from FUND MANAGERS leaves FUNDMANAGES, which 'volatile' rearranges. The question mark flags the ironic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun and games is used ironically for trouble or difficult goings-on.

clue.text: Trees concealing small book

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the small letter goes within the trees

parts.note: palms are trees

explanation.surface: A small volume hidden among trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Social climber's winning way, and skill

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, so winning
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
art can mean skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A social climber's success comes from a winning manner and some talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Social climber' stands for 'has', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person who has risen suddenly in status and behaves arrogantly, a social climber.

clue.text: One of four children aboard liner forming teams

indicators.note: being aboard a ship means being inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword shorthand for a liner
a quad is a quadruplet, one of four children born at one birth

explanation.surface: A quadruplet sails on an ocean liner, where groups are being formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Squads are small organised groups, such as sports teams or work teams.

clue.text: Not reliable at work and insufferable

indicators.note: at work suggests letters being worked on, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unreliable on the job is unbearable.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerable means unbearable, impossible to put up with.

clue.text: Quickly run out by a league member

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricketer from a league side is quickly run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the run-out abbreviation beside the other pieces; in cricket a batsman is 'run out' when the wicket is broken before they complete a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction meaning play at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Carry on suits an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, telling us these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going, said about a quirky outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to keep it going, to carry on with it.

clue.text: Measures of energy in sleep

indicators.note: in tells us the energy letter sits within the word for sleep

parts.note: doss is British slang for sleep, especially rough
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Amounts of energy one gets while sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured quantities of a medicine, so measures in that sense.

clue.text: Fleet docked with sick old animal

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter of the fleet word goes

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A navy fleet is in port while an elderly creature is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like ships tying up, but it means cutting off the tail of ARMADA to leave ARMAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured South American mammal, so an animal.

clue.text: Painting adult touring fashionable island

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the adult word surrounds the others

parts.note: mature means grown-up, adult
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A grown-up visits a trendy isle to paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature is a very small, detailed painting, often a portrait.

clue.text: Instrument for strategic planner around house

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters are placed about the house abbreviation
strategic hints at planned manoeuvring, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tactical planner wants a musical instrument for his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strategic' gives ALPENRN, and 'around' wraps it round the house abbreviation; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn played in the Alps, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Wine firm providing cover for Independent series of columns

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A wine company insures an independent.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof supported by a row of columns.

clue.text: Agree on ring but altered, without question

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Agreeing on a ring, but changed, beyond doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt means certainly, beyond question.

clue.text: The outskirts of Chester in view from loose rocks on hill

indicators.note: in tells us the outer letters go inside the word for view

parts.note: to see something is to view it

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so we take the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: From the edge of Chester you can see a slope of loose stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the mass of loose broken stones covering a hillside or mountain slope.

clue.text: Disturb son, out of bed, eating fish

parts.note: hake is a fish
to be up is to be out of bed

explanation.surface: A boy up and out of bed eats some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake up someone is to upset or disturb them.

clue.text: Unmarried woman supporting soldiers gets careless

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: RE, Royal Engineers, are soldiers
miss is the title for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman backing troops becomes careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent, careless in one's duty.

clue.text: Broken-down old mare's elevated position

indicators.note: broken-down suggests something falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A worn-out old horse is given a lofty status.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank of an earl, a high rank in the peerage.

clue.text: Trace elements surrounding rising general confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so backwards
the clue words surround the answer, which lies within them

explanation.surface: Trace elements around a rising general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like a military leader; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused fight or scramble, general confusion.

clue.text: First-class average set back after a medical condition

indicators.note: after puts the reversed run behind the single letter a
set back means turned backwards, so the run is read in reverse

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written here as AI
mean is the average

explanation.surface: A first-rate average is put back after some kind of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' reverses AIMEAN to NAEMIA, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a medical condition where the blood lacks enough red cells or haemoglobin.

clue.text: Bottle full of soup oddly in sight

indicators.note: a bottle full of something has it inside, so the letters go within the vial

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and other odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A flask of soup is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual describes what can be seen, relating to sight.

clue.text: Mainly unlisted mobile device

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so these letters are rearranged
mainly means most of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: An ex-directory cell phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, a device used in the kitchen or home.

clue.text: Tory tempters falling out in argument

parts.note: Con is the short form for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: falling out suggests things tumbling apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservative tempters are quarrelling during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling out' looks like the definition (a quarrel) but rearranges TEMPTERS into TRETEMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor dispute or awkward disagreement, an argument.
